The issue here is that the `PosixParser` in the Apache Commons CLI library doesn't handle unrecognized tokens starting with '-' properly when `stopAtNonOption` is enabled. The token is simply ignored instead of being processed correctly.

Looking at the `flatten` method of `PosixParser`, it processes each command line token, and if a token starts with a single hyphen '-', it calls `processSingleHyphen(token)`. However, there is no logic in place to handle unrecognized tokens starting with a single hyphen.

To address this issue, we need to enhance the logic in the `flatten` method to handle unrecognized tokens starting with a single hyphen when `stopAtNonOption` is enabled.

Next, I will provide the methods where the fix should be applied.
The issue observed in the `PosixParser` class of the Apache Commons CLI library can be fixed in the following method:

```java
org.apache.commons.cli.PosixParser.flatten(org.apache.commons.cli.Options, java.lang.String[], boolean)
```

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
